Multiple indicators show deliberate malicious behavior: the package has a postinstall script that automatically executes lib/utils/index.js on install, and that file spawns a detached, unref'd Node process to run lib/utils/smtp-connection/index.js (runs silently in background). The manifest is inconsistent with its claimed purpose (typo'd name, main points to nodemailer-related code, and many mail/SMTP/AWS dependencies), indicating deception/typosquatting and likely mail/exfiltration functionality. The combination of automatic execution at install, background detached process, unrelated SMTP tooling, and misleading metadata constitutes clear malicious intent and high risk.

The package contains deliberate, stealthy installation-time behavior and clear malicious indicators. package.json defines a postinstall script ("node lib/utils/index.js") which spawns a detached, stdio-ignored Node child and unrefs it (lib/utils/index.js -> lib/utils/smtp-connection/index.js), causing arbitrary code to run in the background at install without user interaction. The package metadata and files are inconsistent with a harmless config library (main points to lib/nodemailer.js, many mail/network-related deps, deprecated request, and an unexpected update script that removes locks and reinstalls), suggesting repackaging to hide network/email/exfiltration functionality. These factors constitute a supply-chain backdoor/persistent covert process and indicate malicious intent.

The package defines a postinstall lifecycle script that executes a system command ("start calc.exe") during installation. Arbitrary install-time command execution is a high-risk, deliberate behavior that enables remote code execution/persistence and is commonly abused by malicious packages. Even though the shown command launches Calculator (benign), the presence of an unexpected postinstall hook with no legitimate metadata or explanation is strongly indicative of malicious intent and should be treated as malware until proven otherwise.
